# One thing I know is wrong, recorded before the review reads it

`handoff.pack` renders the complete-plan branch as "What is left is the regression, the coverage
measurement and the advance to review". At the tdd stage that is right. At the review stage, where
record 22 was written, all three are already done, so the sentence tells a reviewer to do work the
journal shows finished. The next command line beside it is correct, because it comes from
`NEXT_COMMAND` for the stage.

The cause: `current_slice` counts greens in the current attempt and knows nothing about which stage
the pack is being written at, so the branch that reports a complete plan describes what follows a
complete plan at tdd and nowhere else.

It is not fixed in this attempt. Fixing code after the tdd stage means `harness return --to tdd`,
which is rework and is counted, and the defect is one sentence in a derived document whose next
command is right. The review decides: a finding that returns the ticket, or a waiver with this note
as the reason. Either way the reviewer should not have to find it.

Found by reading the output of record 22, which is the first pack written at the review stage.
